app.name: Binocular Vision Explorer
app.recovered: {{count}} unfinished session(s) from a previous run were recovered and closed.
app.errorBody: The app hit an unexpected error. Your data is saved locally. Reload to continue.

footer.notMedical: For personal and educational use only.
footer.body: A personal, educational tool for exploring how your two eyes work together, for adults. It is not a medical device: it does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any condition, and its numbers are not clinical measurements. If you have an eye condition, follow your clinician’s advice. Not for children. All data stays on this device unless you turn on encrypted sync. Stop if you see double or feel unwell.

intro.pre: Before you start: how are your eyes right now? Answer honestly; this decides whether to train and how hard.
intro.post: Session finished. How do your eyes feel now, compared with before?
intro.stop: You stopped the session. How are you feeling right now?

symptoms.diplopiaHint: How often did you see two images of one thing? (PEDIG / ATS-style scale)
symptoms.confusionHint: Two different images seeming to occupy the same place.
symptoms.submitRedFlag: Save — I reported a red flag

redFlags.legend: Red-flag symptoms (any of these means stop)
redFlags.hint: Tick anything that is NEW or has suddenly worsened.

items.suddenDeviationIncrease: New or sudden increase in eye deviation / turn
items.newDoubleVision: New double vision that was not there before
items.otherNeurological: Other neurological symptoms (weakness, numbness, speech or balance problems)

redFlags.screenTitle: Stop and seek urgent medical attention
redFlags.screenBody: You reported a red-flag symptom. A new or changing deviation, new double vision, a drooping eyelid, unequal pupils, a severe headache or other neurological symptoms can signal something that needs prompt medical assessment. Training is disabled.
redFlags.advice2: Contact an ophthalmologist, orthoptist, or emergency services now, especially if symptoms are sudden or severe.
redFlags.advice3: Bring your exported clinician report if you can.
redFlags.ackIntro: Training stays disabled until you confirm you have read this. This app will never advise you to continue after a red flag.
redFlags.ackCheckbox: I have read this and understand I should seek medical advice before using this app again.
redFlags.ackNote: Note for your records (e.g. who you contacted)

disclaimer.title: Before you begin: safety and what this app is
disclaimer.notTreatment: For personal and educational use only — not diagnosis, not treatment.
disclaimer.statement: A clinical prism test showing alignment at 7Δ tells us the eyes CAN be optically aligned; it does NOT tell us whether breaking your long-standing suppression will be comfortable or could cause double vision. Proceed slowly and stop if anything is uncomfortable. Consult an orthoptist/ophthalmologist.
disclaimer.evidence1: In adults with long-standing strabismus, persistent intractable double vision after alignment is rare: in Kushner (2002, Arch Ophthalmol 120:1498–504) 3 of 424 adults (0.8%) developed it, and patients who did not see double during pre-operative prism testing never developed diplopia afterwards.
disclaimer.evidence2: However, prism testing tends to OVERESTIMATE risk (Khan 2008, J AAPOS 12:46–8), so a reassuring test is helpful but not a guarantee of comfort. Every step in this app is small and reversible; discomfort always steps back.
disclaimer.rule1: Keep your habitual, comfortable head posture. Do not force your head straight; your deviation changes with head tilt and gaze.
disclaimer.rule2: Screen at eye level, fixed viewing distance, stimuli near primary gaze.
disclaimer.rule3: Wear your normal refractive correction UNDER the red-cyan glasses.
disclaimer.rule4: Short sessions (default 10–15 min, max 20), a micro-break every ~5 minutes, a hard daily cap across everything.
disclaimer.rule5: The STOP button is always on screen (or press Esc). Pressing it halts everything and opens a symptom check.
disclaimer.rule6: Double vision in two sessions in a row pauses progression and recommends a consultation. Any red-flag symptom disables training.
disclaimer.photoBody: All modules are limited to well below 3 luminance changes per second, and a client-side detector watches the rendered frames and auto-pauses if content approaches the WCAG 2.3.1 / ITU-R BT.1702 thresholds. If you have a history of photosensitive seizures, do not use this app without medical advice.
disclaimer.privacyBody: Everything you enter stays on this device (browser storage). There are no analytics and no trackers, and nothing is sent anywhere unless you choose to sign in to the optional cloud sync, which uploads only an end-to-end encrypted copy that the server cannot read. You can export and delete your data at any time.
disclaimer.ack1: I am an adult using this for personal and educational purposes, not for diagnosis or treatment.
disclaimer.ack2: I understand that breaking suppression can rarely cause persistent double vision, and that I should stop and consult a clinician if it happens.
disclaimer.ack3: I will stop immediately for double vision, headache, nausea or any red-flag symptom.
disclaimer.ack4: I have discussed (or will discuss) this with an orthoptist / ophthalmologist.

ergonomics.title: Comfort and ergonomics
ergonomics.posture: Sit in your habitual, comfortable head posture. Do not force the head straight.
ergonomics.distance: Screen about 50–70 cm (20–28 in) away and slightly below eye level; keep the same distance you calibrated.
ergonomics.lighting: Adequate, glare-free room lighting. Avoid a dark room with a bright screen.
ergonomics.glasses: Wear your refractive correction under the anaglyph glasses.
ergonomics.zoom: Keep browser zoom at 100%; the calibration assumes it.
ergonomics.breaks: Micro-breaks are automatic. Rest days are fine and never break a streak.
ergonomics.twentyBody: Every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet (6 m) away for 20 seconds. This is general comfort advice; a 2022 Optom Vis Sci study found 20-second breaks are not proven as a therapeutic intervention. It is not part of the training.
ergonomics.afterEffectsBody: Red-cyan glasses can leave transient colour after-images and cause rivalry discomfort. If any double vision or blur persists after a session, rest before driving or other hazardous activity.

training.preInfo: This session will run for up to {{minutes}} minutes. Sit at your calibrated distance ({{distance}} cm), habitual head posture, glasses on.
training.postureNote: Posture / viewing note for this session
training.postureHint: e.g. 'chin down slightly, head tilted left as usual, 60 cm'.
training.breakBody: Look away from the screen, blink, relax your eyes. The session resumes automatically.
training.flashBody: The frame monitor measured about {{rate}} luminance flashes per second over a large area, approaching the photosensitivity threshold. This should not happen with the built-in modules; if it repeats, stop and report it.
training.stoppedBody: Everything is halted and the event has been recorded. Please tell us how you feel before leaving.
training.steppedBackBody: Because you reported discomfort, the visual difficulty of this module has been reduced for next time. That is the intended behaviour, not a failure.
training.progressionLockTitle: Progression paused — please consult an orthoptist
training.progressionLockBody: Double vision was reported in two consecutive sessions. Automatic progression is disabled until you clear it in Settings after discussing with your clinician.
training.afterBody: Take off the glasses and rest your eyes for a minute. If any double vision, blur or colour after-image persists, rest before driving or hazardous activity.
training.pausedBody: The session paused because the window was hidden. The timer is stopped. Resume when you are ready, or use STOP.

game-up.title: Well done — a little harder next time
game-up.body: Game difficulty for the next session: {{game}}/5. Visual difficulty is unchanged.

visual-up.title: Well done — one small visual step next time
visual-up.body: Visual difficulty for the next session: {{value}}. Game difficulty is unchanged.

game-down.title: A little easier next time
game-down.body: This session was hard, so the game difficulty eases to {{game}}/5. That is normal.

training.recalibrateTitle: What you see may differ from your calibration
training.recalibrateBody: You pressed Space several times when the ball looked inside the ring, but by your calibrated prism offset it was still far away. With your glasses on, redo step 6 (prism offset) of the calibration wizard, and check the prism direction you entered.
training.setupMissing: Choose what to watch first (above), then save the check.
training.idleBody: No input for a minute, so the session paused and the timer stopped. Idle time does not count as training. Resume when you are ready.
training.unverifiableTitle: This video cannot be checked for flashing
training.unverifiableBody: The site hosting this video does not allow its frames to be read, so the app cannot watch it for flashing light. Playback has stopped. Use a video file from your own device instead.
training.vrEndedBody: The session is paused and the timer has stopped. Continue, then enter VR again, or press STOP.
training.catchHelp: When a small diamond ◇ appears, press C (or the button).
training.catchLine: One-eye check points ◇ — left eye: {{left}}; right eye: {{right}}.
training.catchFalse: Pressed {{n}} time(s) with no ◇ on screen.
training.doubtfulTitle: Some reports did not match the check points
training.doubtfulBody: This often comes from attention, glasses slipping, or one eye switching off for a moment. It is not a mistake; this session simply does not raise the difficulty.

gate.training-locked: Training is locked after a red-flag report. Open the Red flag page.
gate.disclaimer: The safety disclaimer has not been acknowledged.
gate.no-calibration: No active calibration profile. Run the calibration wizard first.
gate.needs-stable-sessions: Unlocks after 6 completed, comfortable L1/L2 sessions (no double vision, no headache, no STOP).
gate.needs-distinct-days: Those stable sessions must span at least 3 different days.
gate.recent-stop: A STOP event occurred in one of the last 3 sessions.
gate.clinician-agreement: Requires the clinician agreement toggle in Settings.
gate.cap: The daily time cap is reached, or you reported strong symptoms just now. Rest today.
gate.symptoms: You reported strong symptoms in the pre-session check. Please rest today; do not train with double vision, headache or nausea.
gate.needs-full-calibration: Needs the full calibration (about 10 minutes): this stage depends on an exact screen size and distance.

l1.name: Both Eyes On
l1.tagline: Simultaneous perception: a bird for the left eye, a cage for the right.
l1.description: Your left eye sees a bird and your right eye sees a cage; both see a frame. Steer the bird (arrow keys, WASD, touch or gamepad) into the cage and keep it there while the cage drifts. Now and then a small chick appears under the bird — visible to the LEFT eye only. Press Space / Enter / tap when you notice it. Intensity lowers the RIGHT eye's contrast so the left eye is easier to notice; game difficulty changes cage size and drift.
l1.gameDifficulty: Game difficulty: cage size and drift speed (1 = large, slow).

prompt.steer: Steer the bird into the cage

l1.controls: Controls: hold the arrow keys or WASD to fly the bird (hold Shift for fine moves), or click / tap where it should go. Press Space when you see the small chick under the bird.

l2.name: Line Them Up
l2.tagline: Flat fusion: a ball for the left eye, a ring for the right.
l2.description: Your left eye sees a ball and your right eye sees a ring; both see a frame. Put the ball inside the ring and hold. The ring then glides somewhere else. Intensity removes a small percentage of the calibrated prism compensation (only with clinician agreement); game difficulty changes ring size, glide speed and hold time.
l2.gameDifficulty: Game difficulty: ring size, glide speed, hold time.

prompt.align: Move the ball into the ring
prompt.hold: Hold it… the arc fills up
prompt.tooFar: Not close enough yet — move the ball nearer to the ring
prompt.tooFarRecalibrate: Still far from the ring. If it looks inside to you, your prism offset may need recalibrating

l2.controls: Controls: hold the arrow keys or WASD to move the ball (hold Shift for fine moves), or click / tap the ring. If the ball already LOOKS inside the ring, press Space.

l3.name: Don't Lose the Left
l3.tagline: Keep both eyes in the game: stars for the left eye, the basket for the right.
l3.description: Stars fall that only your LEFT eye can see; the basket you move is seen by your RIGHT eye, so catching needs both eyes at once. From game level 2, clouds fall that only the right eye sees: avoid them. Intensity lowers the right eye’s contrast; game difficulty changes speed, star size and basket width.
l3.gameDifficulty: Game difficulty: fall speed, star size, spawn rate, basket width; clouds from level 2.
l3.controls: Controls: hold the left / right arrow keys (or A / D) to move the basket, or click / tap where it should go.

prompt.cloud: That was a cloud. Avoid the clouds

l4.name: Stretch
l4.tagline: Fusional vergence: keep the cross inside the square as the images separate.
l4.description: Your left eye sees a square and your right eye a cross. When the images fuse, the cross sits in the square. The two pictures then slowly move apart, alternating base-out (eyes turn in) and base-in (eyes turn out). Press Space the moment you see two, or the cross leaves the square; the images then come back together, and you press Space again when it is single. This records break and recovery. Divergence is capped at 6Δ, convergence at 12Δ, and there is never any vertical demand. Requires clinician agreement.
l4.gameDifficulty: Game difficulty: ramp speed and target size.
l4.controls: Controls: press Space (or click / tap) once when it doubles, and once more when it is single again. Do not strain; doubling is the expected end of each round.

prompt.rest: Rest. Next round in a moment
prompt.easy: Take it easy: breaks are coming early today. Rest longer between rounds
prompt.stretch: {{dir}} {{delta}}Δ. Press Space when you see two
prompt.recover: {{dir}} {{delta}}Δ. Press Space when it is single again

l5.name: Pop-Out
l5.tagline: Stereo depth: find the square that floats in front of the dots.
l5.description: Random dots hide a square that is only visible with both eyes working together: it floats in front of the field at the top, bottom, left or right. Answer with the arrow keys or by tapping that side. If you cannot tell, press Space; that is a valid answer. The depth difference adapts to find the finest you can see. Not seeing depth is a normal, useful result.
l5.gameDifficulty: Game difficulty: how long each pattern stays (level 1 waits for your answer).
l5.controls: Controls: arrow keys (or tap the side) for where the floating square is; Space if you cannot tell.

prompt.where: Where is the floating square? (Space: cannot tell)
prompt.notSeen: Not this time. That is fine; it gets easier

video.name: Dichoptic Video
video.tagline: Watch your own video with balanced input to both eyes.
video.description: Plays a video from your own device in grey for both eyes. The right eye’s contrast is lowered and soft, slowly moving patches are hidden from one eye or the other, so the whole picture needs both eyes. Brightness is capped and every frame is checked for flashing. Files never leave your device.
video.gameDifficulty: There is no game difficulty here; only the dichoptic strength changes.
video.controls: Just watch. Sit back at your calibrated distance with your glasses on. STOP or Esc ends the session.

prompt.tapToPlay: Press Space or tap to start playback
prompt.ended: The video ended. You can STOP the session now
prompt.error: This video cannot be played here. Try another file (MP4 / WebM)

setup.title: Choose what to watch
setup.safetyBody: Pick calm content: avoid flashing scenes, fast action and shaky camera work. In a dichoptic video trial, headache was reported by 14.3% of users (vs 1.7% with glasses alone), usually mild and brief. Stop and rest if you get a headache, nausea or eye strain that lasts.
setup.fileHint: MP4 or WebM work best. The file is read locally and never uploaded.
setup.urlHint: A direct link to a video file whose server allows cross-origin access. Many sites do not; then playback stops because the frames cannot be checked. Safari has had bugs here too.
setup.streamingSite: YouTube and Bilibili videos cannot be used for training: their players do not allow processing, and downloading them is against their terms. Use "Plain viewing" below if you just want to watch.
setup.plainBody: Opens a YouTube, Bilibili or other link in a new tab for ordinary viewing. Nothing is processed and it does not count as training.
setup.sceneHint: Slow, flash-free scenes drawn live by the app. Nothing to download.

brock.name: Brock String
brock.tagline: Vergence awareness: see the two strings cross at the bead you look at.
brock.description: A string runs from near (bottom) to far (top) with three beads. Each eye sees the string from its own side, so when you really look at a bead the two strings seem to cross there, like an X. If one string fades, that eye has switched off: blink and look again. The highlighted bead moves from near to far and back. Press Space when the strings cross at it, and Arrow Down when one string disappears. Horizontal only; the near bead asks for at most the set convergence and the far bead for at most 2Δ of divergence. Requires clinician agreement.
brock.gameDifficulty: Game difficulty: time per bead and bead size.
brock.controls: Controls: look at the ringed bead. Space (or click / tap) when the strings cross there; Arrow Down when one string disappears.

look.near: Look at the NEAR bead. Space when the strings cross there
look.middle: Look at the MIDDLE bead. Space when the strings cross there
look.far: Look at the FAR bead. Space when the strings cross there

prompt.blink: One string faded: blink, relax, and look at the bead again

reading.name: Two-Eye Reading
reading.tagline: Read a calm text whose words are split between your eyes.
reading.description: Alternate words (in Chinese, alternate characters) go to the left and the right eye, so the text only reads as a whole with both eyes. Your left eye keeps full contrast; the right eye is dimmed as in L1. Read at your own pace and turn the page with Space or Arrow Right (Arrow Left goes back). If words keep disappearing, press Arrow Down: that eye is being switched off. The passages are short original texts written for this app.
reading.controls: Controls: Space / Arrow Right (or tap the right half) = next page; Arrow Left (left half) = back; Arrow Down = words missing.

prompt.read: Page {{page}} of {{pages}}. Space for the next page
prompt.last: Last page of this text. Space starts the next one
prompt.missing: Words missing: blink, relax your eyes, and keep reading

passages.p1: Morning light comes slowly through the kitchen window. The kettle hums, a cup waits on the table, and the street outside is still quiet. A bird lands on the fence, looks around, and leaves again. There is no hurry yet. The day has not asked for anything, and for a few minutes it is enough to watch the steam rise and fade into the warm air.
passages.p2: The old harbour is busy only in the early hours. Small boats come back with the tide, ropes are thrown and tied, and gulls circle above the nets. By noon the water is calm again. Children sit on the stone steps with their feet over the edge, counting the fish that turn silver in the shallow green water below them.
passages.p3: A path climbs gently through the pine forest. The ground is soft with needles, and every step is quiet. Now and then the trees open, and a valley appears far below, with a river drawn in silver across the fields. Walkers stop here to drink water and rest. Nobody talks much; the wind in the branches says enough.
passages.p4: In the library the hours pass slowly. Pages turn, a chair creaks, and the clock above the door keeps its steady pace. Outside it has started to rain, but the windows are tall and the light is soft. On the long table someone has left a map of the sea, open at an island with a name that is hard to pronounce.
passages.p5: The market opens before sunrise. Tables are set out in rows, and soon they are covered with apples, onions, bread and bright flowers. People greet each other by name. A woman weighs tomatoes on an old brass scale, and a boy carries crates that are almost as tall as he is. By ten o'clock the coffee stall has a long, patient queue.
passages.p6: On clear nights the stars seem close above the hills. Away from the town lights, the sky fills slowly as your eyes adjust: first a few bright points, then hundreds, then a faint band of light across the dark. The air is cool and smells of grass. It is easy to forget the time and simply look up, one star after another.

metrics.farConfirms: Space pressed too far from the ring
metrics.meanTimeToCrossMs: Mean time to see the crossing (ms)

overview.title: Overview
overview.trainingLocked: Training is disabled after a red-flag report.
overview.progressionLocked: Progression paused after double vision in consecutive sessions.
overview.capReachedBody: No more training today across any module. Rest is part of the plan.
overview.restDays: Rest days are never penalised. Consistency matters more than volume.
overview.phase2Hint: L3–L5 and the video module arrive in Phase 2 and unlock only after stable, comfortable L1–L2 sessions.
overview.meterLabel: {{done}} minutes trained today, {{planned}} planned, daily limit {{cap}} minutes
overview.nextHint: {{minutes}} min. Put your glasses on first.
overview.allDone: Today's plan is done. Rest is part of training.
overview.setUpHint: About 10 minutes. You need your red-cyan glasses and a bank card.
overview.planEmpty: Nothing is in today’s plan. Add a module below, or rest today.
overview.unlocksWith: Unlocks after comfortable sessions on earlier stages.

module.intensityHint: Low / Medium / High map to concrete values. They never jump: at most one small step per session, and discomfort steps back immediately.
module.stepRule: Max step per session: {{step}}. Step back on discomfort: {{back}}.
module.clinicianRequired: Increasing this metric requires the clinician agreement toggle (Settings).
module.minutesHint: Between {{min}} and {{max}} minutes; the global daily cap still applies.
module.intensityStepHint: The target is approached one step per session, never in a jump.

settings.title: Settings
settings.rendererHint: Anaglyph Canvas 2D is the default. WebGL adds per-channel gamma. Side-by-side is a preview for a future VR path.
settings.cyclotorsion: Apply the per-eye rotation from the calibration (cyclotorsion compensation)
settings.cyclotorsionHint: Off by default. Only enable if your clinician agrees; torsional misalignment can itself cause diplopia.
settings.clinicianHint: Vergence work and any reduction of the prism compensation are gated behind this toggle. Turn it on only after agreeing a plan with your orthoptist / ophthalmologist.
settings.clinicianToggle: My clinician agrees to vergence / offset-reduction work
settings.dataHint: Export a JSON backup or import one. Nothing leaves the device unless you export it or turn on the encrypted cloud sync.
settings.importDone: Imported {{sessions}} sessions and {{calibrations}} profiles ({{skipped}} invalid rows skipped).
settings.resetConfirm: This permanently deletes all local data. Sure?

diagnostics.title: Error log
diagnostics.hint: Errors the app ran into are kept here, on this device only, so a problem can be traced later. They contain no training results, symptom answers or anything you typed. Nothing is sent anywhere.
diagnostics.includeInExport: Include the error log in the backup file (for troubleshooting)

ppi.intro: Hold a standard bank/ID card (ISO ID-1, 85.6 × 54 mm) against the screen and adjust the rectangle until its width matches the card's long edge exactly.
ppi.zoomDetected: The page appears zoomed. Reset zoom to 100% before calibrating.
ppi.implausible: That gives an implausible pixel density (outside 50–400 PPI). Check the zoom level and try again.

distance.label: Viewing distance (cm)
distance.hint: Measure eye-to-screen with a tape, or use roughly arm's length (about 60 cm). Keep this distance for every session.
distance.implausible: Enter a distance between 30 and 120 cm.

glasses.intro: Put on the red-cyan glasses (over your normal correction). Cover or close your RIGHT eye so only your LEFT eye is looking.
glasses.question: Which square looks bright and clear to your LEFT eye?
glasses.result: Left eye sees the {{left}} channel; right eye sees the {{right}} channel.
glasses.cvdHint: Colour-vision differences are fine: the glasses separate the eyes by filter, not by colour. If the red square looks much darker (common with red-green colour deficiency), the contrast-balance step evens the brightness out.

ghost.title: Ghosting (crosstalk)
ghost.intro: A disc is drawn for the LEFT eye only. Cover your left eye: if you still see a faint disc with the right eye, reduce that channel's gain until it nearly disappears. Keep the background dark; red filters leak green.
ghost.backgroundHint: Keep it near black. A little gray can hide colour fringes on some screens.

mono.introLeft: Cover your RIGHT eye. A triangle is drawn for the LEFT eye only.
mono.introRight: Now cover your LEFT eye. A square is drawn for the RIGHT eye only.
mono.notVisible: One eye cannot see its channel. Check the glasses orientation, screen brightness and the channel mapping above before continuing.

worth.intro: Both eyes open, habitual head posture. Four dots are drawn: one for the red-channel eye, two for the cyan-channel eye, and one for both.
worth.question: How many dots do you see?

results.left-suppression: 3 dots: only the right eye’s dots
results.right-suppression: 2 dots: only the left eye’s dots

explain.fusion: You saw the dots of both eyes combined.
explain.left-suppression: You saw only the dots meant for the right eye. The training starts by bringing in the left eye’s picture.
explain.right-suppression: You saw only the dots meant for the left eye.
explain.alternating: What you saw switched between the two eyes’ dots.

worth.diplopiaCaution: You are seeing double with these glasses on. This is exactly the situation where caution matters: it may be uncomfortable and could persist. Do not force fusion. Continue only with tiny steps, stop at any discomfort, and discuss this result with your orthoptist. You can stop the wizard now.

prism.intro: Enter the prism measurement from your clinical exam. It seeds the initial virtual-prism offset; the next step fine-tunes it by perception.
prism.fusion: With the prism in place you…
prism.fusionHint: As reported during the clinical test.
prism.conversion: {{delta}}Δ ≈ {{deg}}°. At {{distance}} cm that is {{cm}} cm on screen = {{px}} px with your calibrated PPI.
prism.useClinical: Use a clinical prism measurement as the starting offset
prism.seed: Seed the offset from this measurement

offset.fineIntro: Your left eye sees a cross, your right eye a ring. Nudge the LEFT eye's image until the cross sits inside the ring while you keep your habitual head posture. If the seeded direction feels wrong, flip it. If you cannot get them together comfortably, leave it approximate and stop; do not strain.
offset.readout: Left-eye offset: dx {{dx}} px, dy {{dy}} px (≈ {{delta}}Δ at your distance).
offset.torsionCaution: Superior-oblique palsy often produces a few degrees of excyclotorsion. Rotating one eye's image can help fusion but can also cause torsional diplopia. Default is 0°. Adjust only in 0.5° steps and stop at any discomfort. This rotation is applied only if enabled in Settings.
offset.torsionEnableHint: Rotation is stored in the profile but ignored until 'cyclotorsion' is enabled in Settings.
offset.keyboardHint: Tip: the arrow keys also nudge the left-eye image on this step.

contrast.intro: Two bars: the left one for your LEFT eye, the right one for your RIGHT eye. Say which looks stronger / brighter. The right eye's contrast steps down until they look equal (Mansouri / Thompson / Hess balance point). Left stays at 100%.
contrast.current: Right-eye contrast now {{value}}%. {{trials}} judgements so far, {{reversals}} reversals.
contrast.doneBody: Right-eye contrast at which both looked equal: {{value}}%. Training starts here and raises it very slowly toward 100%.

trends.title: Progress
trends.noData: No sessions yet for this measure.
trends.minutesSub: All modules combined. Rest days are fine.
trends.balanceSub: Rises as the two eyes work more evenly (100% = no dimming).
trends.offsetSub: How far from the calibrated position the ball looked aligned. Lower is closer.
trends.vergenceSub: Demand at which the image doubled, and where it fused again.
trends.stereoSub: Finest depth difference seen, in arcseconds. Lower is finer.
trends.diplopiaSub: From the post-session check: never, rarely, sometimes, often, always.

report.title: Training summary
report.disclaimer: Self-recorded data from a personal, educational tool — not a medical device and not a clinical measurement. Numbers are rough screen-based approximations (anaglyph glasses) and cannot replace an eye examination.
report.viewingValue: {{cm}} cm from the screen, {{ppi}} pixels per inch
report.virtualPrismValue: ≈ {{delta}}Δ on the left eye (dx {{dx}} px, dy {{dy}} px), rotation {{rot}}°
report.balanceValue: Right eye at {{value}}% looked equal to the left eye at 100%
report.diplopiaSessions: Sessions with double vision (sometimes or more)
report.headacheSessions: Sessions with moderate or severe headache
report.noSymptoms: No symptoms were reported in this period.
report.checksIntro: The same short self-check every week, with no feedback and no score. Baseline = the first two self-checks in the period. Not a clinical measurement.
report.measuresIntro: From the training games themselves. They also improve with practice, so read them together with the weekly self-check above.
report.subtitle: Your own records, to keep — or to show your clinician if you wish.

check.title: Weekly self-check
check.intro: A short self-check, the same every week: four steps, about 4 minutes. There is no score and no feedback, so your own record shows how what you see changes over the weeks — apart from getting better at the games. It is not a clinical test. Wear your glasses and sit at your usual distance.
check.how: First a quick symptom check. Then: Worth 4-dot, lining up a cross and a ring (twice), contrast balance, and finding a floating square in random dots. Press STOP (or Esc) at any time.
check.postTitle: How do you feel after the self-check?
check.alignIntro: The left eye sees the cross, the right eye the ring. Move the cross until it sits exactly in the middle of the ring, then confirm. Take your time.
check.alignKeys: Arrow keys move the cross by 2 px; hold Shift for fine steps.
check.stereoIntro: A square floats in front of the dots, near the top, bottom, left or right. Answer where you see it, or "Can't tell". There is no feedback; the patterns get harder as you go and stop by themselves.
check.stoppedBody: The self-check stopped. What you recorded so far is kept. Please tell us how you feel.
check.baselineNote: This is one of your first two self-checks: together they form your baseline. Later self-checks are compared with it.
check.compareNote: Compared with your baseline (the first two self-checks) and your previous check.

chartSub.alignment: Where the cross looked centred, in Δ away from the calibrated position.
chartSub.balance: Right-eye contrast that looked equal to the left eye.
chartSub.stereo: Smallest depth difference you saw, in arcseconds (on this screen).

check.meaning: Small week-to-week changes are normal. These are your own observations on a screen, not clinical measurements; if something changes noticeably, talk to your clinician.
check.never: Not done yet. The first two self-checks set your baseline.
check.why: Your own weekly record, apart from game scores.

goal.title: This week
goal.reached: Weekly goal reached. Anything more is a bonus, and rest days are fine.
goal.outOfReach: This week is short on days, and that is fine. Pick up again next week.
goal.progress: {{done}} of {{goal}} days so far, {{left}} day(s) left this week.
goal.daysHint: Days count, not minutes: short regular sessions help more than one long one.
goal.reminderHint: Download a reminder for your own calendar (phone or computer). A web app cannot reliably send notifications on its own; your calendar can.
goal.icsBody: A few minutes of binocular training. Wear your red/cyan glasses. Stop if you see double or feel unwell.

backup.neverTitle: Your training data has no backup yet
backup.body: Everything is stored only in this browser. Clearing site data or a new device would lose it. A backup file keeps it safe.
backup.title: Backup and storage
backup.intro: Your data stays on this device unless you save a backup file (or turn on the encrypted cloud sync under Account). Keep one somewhere safe.
backup.persistNo: Not guaranteed: the browser may clear it to free space
backup.persistGranted: The browser will keep your data.
backup.persistDenied: The browser did not agree. Keep backups, or install the app (Add to Home screen) and try again.
backup.encryptHint: Protects the file with a passphrase (AES-256, key from PBKDF2 with 600 000 rounds). Without the passphrase nobody can read it, including you: there is no recovery. Write it down.
backup.folderHint: Chrome and Edge can save a backup file to a folder you choose after every session (for example a synced folder). The browser asks again for permission now and then.

folder.needs-permission: The browser needs your permission again: click "Back up now".
folder.failed: The backup could not be written to the folder.

backup.importNeedsPass: This backup is encrypted. Enter its passphrase to import it.
backup.wrongPass: Wrong passphrase, or the file was changed.

vr.available: A VR headset is available: choose "webxr" to train in the headset (beta: L1, L2 and L5).
vr.unavailable: No VR headset found in this browser (webxr needs a headset browser such as Quest Browser).
vr.breakText: Break — look into the distance ({{seconds}} s)
vr.flashText: Paused for safety. Take off the headset.
vr.pausedText: Paused. Take off the headset to continue on the page.
vr.enterTitle: This session runs in your VR headset.
vr.error: VR could not start. Check the headset and try again, or choose another renderer in Settings.
vr.fallbackNoHeadset: VR is chosen, but no headset is available: this session uses the red/cyan glasses instead.
vr.fallbackModule: This module is not available in VR yet: this session uses the red/cyan glasses instead.
vr.preInfo: VR session (beta): at most {{minutes}} minutes. Stay seated. Squeeze a controller grip to STOP at any time; the trigger works like Space.
vr.comfortWarn: Headsets can cause dizziness, nausea or eye strain, even with still pictures. Stop at the first sign. Do not use VR if you have had seizures or are prone to motion sickness without asking your clinician first.
vr.comfort1: Sit down, in a safe space. The picture stays fixed in the room; nothing moves you.
vr.comfort2: VR sessions last at most 10 minutes, shorter than on screen.
vr.comfort3: Squeeze a controller grip to STOP. Taking the headset off pauses the session.
vr.comfort4: Adjust the headset lens distance (IPD) to your eyes before starting.
vr.comfort5: After the session, the usual symptom check asks about nausea and double vision.

consistency.title: Report consistency
consistency.intro: Small diamonds ◇ appear to one eye at a time during training (in L1, the chick). Seeing them shows that eye’s picture is getting through; presses without one show how reliable the reports are.
consistency.chartSub: Share of the one-eye ◇ seen in each session.

reasons.presses-without-symbol: Pressed more often without a ◇ than with one.
reasons.left-missed: The session’s results needed both eyes, but most left-eye ◇ were missed.
reasons.right-missed: The session’s results needed both eyes, but most right-eye ◇ were missed.

quick.startHint: Estimated screen size, glasses check, then your first session.
quick.title: Quick start
quick.intro: Three short steps and you can start. The screen size is estimated; the full calibration (about 10 minutes, with a bank card) can follow any time and is needed for some later stages.
quick.diagonal: Screen diagonal in inches (if you know it)
quick.diagonalHint: Leave empty to use a typical size for this device.
quick.distance: Distance from your eyes to the screen (cm)
quick.distanceHint: Roughly arm’s length. Keep the same distance every time.
quick.estimate: Estimate: about {{ppi}} pixels per inch ({{diagonal}}-inch screen).
quick.knowsPrism: I know my prism value from an eye examination
quick.noPrism: Without it, both eyes’ pictures start in the same place; the full calibration lets you fine-tune.
quick.afterwards: Afterwards: run the full calibration for a measured screen size, the contrast balance and Worth 4-dot.
quick.go: Save and start the first session
quick.bannerTitle: You are using the quick setup
quick.bannerBody: Screen size and contrast balance are estimates. The full calibration takes about 10 minutes and unlocks every stage.

problem.title: Report a problem
problem.intro: This is everything that would be sent: app version, browser and the recent errors — no training data and nothing you typed elsewhere. Nothing is sent unless you choose to.
problem.githubHint: Opens GitHub in a new tab with the report filled in; you need a GitHub account and can still edit or cancel there.
problem.noticeTitle: The app ran into an error
problem.noticeBody: Your data is safe. You can report it so it can be fixed.

account.title: Account and sync
account.intro: Sign in to keep the same records on several devices. Your training data is encrypted on this device before upload; the server only stores ciphertext.
account.notConfiguredTitle: Cloud sync is not set up
account.notConfigured: This copy of the app has no cloud sync configured, so everything stays on this device. Use backup files (Settings) to move data between devices.
account.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. Used only to sign in; it cannot decrypt your data.
account.resetSent: If an account exists for this email, a password-reset link is on its way.
account.confirmEmail: Check your email and confirm the address, then sign in.
account.signedOut: Signed out. The data on this device stays here.
account.createIntro: Choose a sync passphrase (at least {{n}} characters), different from your account password. It encrypts your data before upload and never leaves this device. It cannot be recovered: write it down.
account.unlockIntro: This account already has encrypted data. Enter the sync passphrase you chose on your first device.
account.wrongSyncPass: That sync passphrase does not open the encrypted data.
account.syncCreated: Your data is encrypted and stored in the cloud.
account.syncDone: Synced. New from other devices: {{sessions}} session(s), {{symptomChecks}} check(s), {{assessments}} self-check(s).
account.received: Last sync brought {{sessions}} session(s), {{symptomChecks}} symptom check(s) and {{assessments}} self-check(s) from other devices.
account.forgetKey: Forget the passphrase on this device
account.deleteHint: Deleting the cloud copy does not touch the data on your devices. Use it if you lost the sync passphrase, then set a new one.
account.privacy1: Your email address and a password hash (to sign in), handled by Supabase.
account.privacy2: One encrypted file: compressed and encrypted on your device (AES-256-GCM). Without your sync passphrase it cannot be read — not by the server, not by the app’s owner.
account.privacy3: When and from which kind of device (e.g. "Chrome · Windows") it was last updated.
